item.title: The Mother of Meteorites
item.description: Meteorites that reproduce like sea turtles.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Extraterrestrial animals that fly through space with telekinesis, feeding on planetary ring systems and other space debris and adding the matter to their rocky shells.
  • Look like rocks with organs inside, like Pyura chilensis. Could even use that animal for the picture, possibly.
  • Possibly silicon-based and composed entirely of biological rocks, if that's semi-plausible.
  • Reproduce through parthenogenesis, since they rarely cross paths in space. When ready to reproduce, they fall back to the planet of their birth, burning up in the atmosphere but leaving behind several metallic eggs in the crater.
  • After hatching, the babies consume some of the rocks in the area to build their shells before returning to space.

Central Narrative: The Containment Procedures involve traveling to locations of meteorite impacts to ensure that no civilians find any eggs, monitoring of asteroids to identify possible instances and predict their impact times and locations, and preventing NASA from detecting them. The description provides information on their biology and behavior. There's an addendum at the end chronicling observations of some captive instances and an experiment to see how they do in a non-space environment with gravity. No big twist.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is one of those strange, but not really dangerous, anomalies that does a good job of conveying the weirdness and wonder of the SCPverse without being horrific or grimdark. It's also kind of cute, I guess.

Additional Notes: Do I need to make them more dangerous? If so, I can just make it so the mother survives the impact and grows larger each time, meaning that her periodic returns to the same planet cause increasingly worse disasters at regular intervals. Then the procedures would involve destroying any recovered eggs, and possibly destroying any particularly large instances likely to return to Earth in the near future. I'd really rather leave them as quirky, strange, and kinda cute things that aren't especially dangerous or horrifying, though.

item.title: Mr. Miss - Idea for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unknown

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout + test logs

Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX, often called "Mr. Miss" is a human male displaying anomalous properties. The effects of this anomaly is twofold, such that:

1. Any action brought against entity will inevitably "miss", be it by a human, animal, object, etc.
2. Any action brought by entity against another will inevitably "miss", be it against a human, animal, object, etc.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
The article will detail via test logs the deeper intricacies of of the anomaly. This includes:
1. The anomaly seems to work by way of an unknown reality bending method.
2. The entity has little to no control over the anomaly and anomaly will work automatically without any conscious effort to do so.
3. For unknown reason, the anomaly seems to try an minimize both the amount of reality being bent and how observable its affects are to onlookers; but only when it is possible to do so. For example, a bullet fired at entities head from range would be adjusted as minimally possible so that both the entity is not hit and that the assailant will not grow suspicious. If the entity were to be potentially crushed by a large inescapable object, anomaly may go as far as to bend reality so that entity may phase through object.
4. The above rules carry over to any subject or object that the entity may attempt to act against themselves.

The article will also describe a brief origin of how the entity may have obtained it's anomalous properties (in short, after being separated from military squadron, entity manifested anomaly after eating a strangely patterned salamander while surviving in woods. Foundation agents in military noted anomaly and entity came willingly )

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

While theoretically invincible, by nature of it's anomaly the entity poses not direct physical threat to any foundation staff. That said, should the entity become non-complient or attempt to escape, subduing it would be difficult as physical force would be ineffective, as well as that the mere act of attempting to contain the entity could be perceived as a threat against it's person resulting in unpredictable anomalous effects.

Aditional Notes: I am aware of the stigma against anomalous humans as they can sometimes come off as superhero-ish. Any feedback to help avoid this pitfall is welcome.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.description: "Given enough time, and with enough of us trying to look into this void, something crawled out of it."
item.content:encoded:
A tale about SCP-3930, and what happened when something crawled out of it.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard (black highlighter theme to match SCP-3930's style)

Elevator Pitch: A tale of terror, paranoia, and suspense told from the terrified perspective of Dr Vasiliev as he desperately tries to figure out how to destroy this entity with minimal loss of life, all while distracted by a barely perceptible noise that is ringing in his ears.

+ Open Narrative +
- Close Narrative -

Central Narrative:
- Dr Vasiliev is monitoring SCP-39301 and notices a noise from the void, and something at its forefront. As he watches, the thing at its forefront drags itself out of the void and starts moving towards the Site
- Dr Vasiliev has just enough time to notify everyone on-Site that something is coming before it arrives
- The tale follows Dr Vasiliev as he runs and hides through the Site
- As he dismisses possible solutions, the tale's perspective switches between Dr Vasiliev (who is running and hiding) and various other scientists (who are running and are caught)
- When the scientists are caught, their perspective focuses on one of their five main senses and how the sense is distorted as they become a pattern screamer. Hearing is the only one not mentioned…
- Dr Vasiliev finds a radio and hears voices in the static that tell him there can be no more than ten, after which he tells everyone to gather in the cafeteria
- Dr Vasiliev counts 11 people and reluctantly notifies them that one of them has to die to stop the entity
- As they are having a discussion, the door where Dr Vasiliev and one other scientist are standing bursts open
- The perspective switches to the scientist next to Dr Vasilev as that scientist is attacked, focusing on hearing. However, the perspective switches back to Dr Vasiliev before things get weird
- As the scientist dies and the entity faces Dr Vasiliev, he realises the sound he's hearing is also coming from the entity
- The entity (and the sound) begins to slowly disappear, and as they do Dr Vasiliev realises what he's been hearing this whole time: the faintest, almost imperceptible sound of screaming

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The name of the article (and probably the article this tale is associated with) would draw the reader's attention, and the subject (scientists hunted by the unfathomable) would also hook the reader in.

Additional Notes: None

That's it for now. Thanks for reading, and hopefully this is intriguing!
P.S Sorry about that Zyn

Footnotes
1. It wasn't called that back then, but I'm still thinking of a name.

item.title: Nostalgic House. Seeking Greenlights.
item.content:encoded:
I need greenlights for this. This is an old concept that I'm coming back to after a long, long time and I still really want to make it into a thing.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A house with various anomalous properties. To say a few:

+ show block
– hide block

The house always bears the appearance of the viewer's childhood home, but will be in poor condition, as if it is many decades old. If multiple subjects view the house at once, it will stay resemblant of the first viewer's childhood home. Entities inside also behave this way.

The inside of the house1 consists of hallways, large rooms, staircases both up and down, and [DATA EXPUNGED].

As some subjects travel farther through SCP-XXXX-1, their features will become more like those of a child; they will become shorter, and their behaviour and patterns of speech will become more childlike. Most of those affected by this had bad childhoods.

Once the subject travels an unknown distance, they will encounter a room identical to the subject's childhood nursery. Upon entering the 'nursery', the subject will see visions of themselves between the ages of 2 and 8, playing by themselves or with a parent. After approximately 30 seconds of visual contact with the inside of the room, the vision of themselves will vanish. At this point, an entity known as SCP-XXXX-22 will approach the subject and tap them on the shoulder. Once the subject turns around, SCP-XXXX-2 will close the door to the room. SCP-XXXX-2 and the subject will both vanish. Recovering them is impossible. This only happens if the subject is alone.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is discovered by Dr. Mary Turner, an Assistant Researcher at Site-17, on break. She reported its existence to Site Command, which resulted in them sending MTF Phi-7 "Home Improvement" inside. They find an SCP-XXXX-33 instance in the form of a dog. It attacks one of their agents. The rest of the agents retreat. Later, Dr. Turner is assigned to SCP-XXXX. A month later, SCP-XXXX-2 breaches containment. During the breach, SCP-XXXX-2 locks itself in a room with Dr. █████ ███████ and disappears with her, later remanifesting inside SCP-XXXX-1. Dr. ███████ was never recovered. Dr. Turner proposes the reclassification of SCP-XXXX as Euclid. SCP-XXXX-2 ceases to attempt breaching containment, so SCP-XXXX stays Safe classified.

Hook: It's a creepy nostalgic childhood home with a reality-bending butler. It's not every day you go on the wiki and find one of those.

Additional Notes: Alright, so I'm trying to make a memetic hazard house that turns people into kids and has a reality-bending parent. Did I do it right?

Footnotes
1. Designated SCP-XXXX-1.
2. A humanoid entity 2.5 meters in height, also known as The Lost Parent.
3. Entities that take form of subject's childhood pets and toys. They either attack or be affectionate.

item.title: Seeking greenlights
item.description: The space in-between what was and what will.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional/ exploration

Elevator Pitch: What happens when you put a space in between the past, and the present? This is the basis of Liminal spaces and what this SCP is based on. So what happens when you put someone in a dimension of nothing but liminal spaces? How would they affect someone and what if they could spread if they weren't monitored?

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this SCP to show liminal spaces activate memories and experiences we have never had, SCP-XXXX is a rotting wooden door attached to a concrete floor and concrete wall that has been ripped out of its original place, the inside being bigger than it's exterior. The inside contains a series of endless hallways with wooden doors lining each wall that lead deeper into SCP-XXXX with entryways to the next hallway every 10 miles. Each door that has never been unopened before leads to a completely random room correlating to the subject's suppressed memories, intentions, and or emotions, often being broken in ways like repeating sections or missing areas entirely, or random items in said rooms. The door must always stay closed for it is opened and consistently stayed open for longer than 20 minutes, the warped reality will spread to everything, including organic matter, concrete is found to be the least affected by this property. Exposure longer than 4 hours leads to a steady loss of direction.

+ show block
– hide block

So, what happens when someone is put inside for long periods of time? This is about a D class being put into SCP-XXXX for longer than a week. This leads to the D class to end up remembering who he is, his real name, and just why he was put on death row and forced to be a test subject in the foundation. This leads to acceptance of his actions, knowing that the foundation will mostly cut him off for retaining this information, he must come to terms knowing that he will either never make it out of here, or be killed by the foundation.

hook/Attention-Grabber: These spaces have popped up on the internet all over, oftentimes people saying it feels oddly familiar with an overwhelming sense of deja vu. This SCP takes this idea of Liminal Spaces and turns it into an endless expanse of repeating rooms and endless, useless mazes of warped reality and turns it into an eerie dimension of random exploration.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP and I am bound to make mistakes as an inexperienced Author, be as harsh or factual as you need. I want to do an SCP right.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 20 words over. ~Zyn

item.title: Crown of need (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An Euclid SCP (scp-xxx) that consists of an indestructible object (crown/trophy/statuette, i haven't decided yet) that has the ability teleport between any of two persons (hosts), upon the receiving host performing a specific ritual. Scp-xxx will also, trough unknown methods, transfer a seemingly random amount of money from the sender host to the receiver.

  • list item

Scp-xxx's ritual description can be relatively easily found in the internet, usually in the form of ads, like: "MAKE A LOT OF MONEY WITH ONE WEIRD METHOD". It is unknown if these ads are generated by scp-xxx or another party.

  • list item

The ritual will change after the hosts rotate.

  • list item

People with low income tend to have more brand losses as sender hosts, but this is not reliable enough to make predictions

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
The article will consist of research logs of the foundation trying to determine what dictates the amount of money that is transferred. The foundation will treat these research with a distinct urgency, that's because scp-xxx will withdraw copious amounts of money from the foundation while in its custody, between 5 - 50 million (i'm open to sugestions regarding this) generally a week after its containment.

Taking in account the worrying financial damage the foundation is undertaking while trying to contain scp-xxx, a deadline to cease scp-xxx containment has been set to avoid the foundation going bankrupt.

One foundation researcher was able to produce 100$, unfortunately the researched died in an unrelated accident. Since then, more hosts are being used to determine what caused this drop in transferred money .

Eventually the foundation found a D-class personnel refugy from [REDACTED] that produced a similar amount of money.

The rest will be available at the final draft.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
This should be an interesting scp since it poses more of a practical instead of being outright harmful to people.

Additional Notes:
English is not my main language, so i might need extra help in grammar stuff

item.title: The connected rooms
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes, but currently looking for feedback more than anything

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unknown

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, description, discovery, and test logs. Maybe even some mentions of SCPs that were exterminated using this SCP. Potential for cross-links.

Elevator Pitch: Two identical large white cubes with doors are on exact opposite sides of the world. They are not connected, yet they lead to the same room with 2 doors inside. The doors inside the room lead to the doors found on the cubes.

No electronic devices work inside the room. Subjects put in the room for 10 minutes or longer describe feelings of being watched. After 20 minutes, they fall into a panic and try to escape the room saying something about how they know that if they don't leave, then they will die. There is no direct threat to them, but they describe having the feeling that they know they are going to die.

+ show block
– hide block

Once the victims fall into a panic, the doors to the room (and on the cubes, as stated previously) will close if left open and will lock by themselves. The victim will not be able to leave and after 2 minutes, the doors will unlock and the victim will have disappeared.

Central Narrative: Two friends in the area of Antofagasta, Chile, Javiera Soto and Mia Muños, found the cube and realized that they could pass through the doors to go to Wuzhou City, Guangxi, China. They decided to leap at the opportunity and took many trips there, keeping everything to themselves. That was until Mia decided to use the room for an extended meditation period. She recorded everything.

The recording shows that Mia put her phone outside the cube with the door open and recorded an instructional meditation video. At around the 11 minute mark, she opened one of her eyes, looked around without moving anything but her eye, and said "Remember to push all feelings out of your body, as this time is purely for meditation." Then, at around the 20 minute mark, she opens her eyes very suddenly, fearful, as the door in front of her closes and locks itself. The camera captured two minutes of her yelling from inside the box and trying to open the door before the door could be heard unlocking itself. The door was not opened. There was silence.

Javiera found the recording and took it to local authorities, telling them everything that she knew. Then, The Foundation stepped in.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think it would be cool having some more non-euclidian geometry on the site, plus some actively hostile non-euclidian structures.

Aditional Notes: None

item.title: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, history, Foundation politics

Page Layout (Optional): Classic SCP layout; addenda will include a neutralisation proposal, interview with site-director, and a containment breach. This addenda will be presented in a novel style in the form an official document/folder (for an idea, see SCP-5859.)

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation hears reports of people becoming infected with a seemingly untreatable strain of the Bubonic Plague. MTF Beta-7 ("Maz Hatters") are deployed to control the situation. What follows is a deconstruction of the Foundations M.O: Secure, Contain, Protect.

► Additional details
▼ Additional details

Central Narrative: The SCP in question is a the corpse of a 14th century Parisian male discovered deep within the catacombs of Paris (stumbled upon by Patient-Zero, an overeager urban explorer). Due to the anti-Semitic slur scorched into the corpse's chest, Foundation historians have theorised that the corpse was murdered due to the Christian persecution of the Jewish populace admist the onset of the Bubonic Plague.

The corpse is the cause of the outbreak. Exposure results in infection from an anomalous strain of Yersinia pestis. Initial stages of infection operate much the same way as a non-anomalous strain. However, rather than dying, the later stages of the anomalous strain cause those who are infected to lose higher cognitive brain function, who are then compelled to spread the disease.

Once the SCP is secured, the plot follows the project lead, Dr. Stephen Miller, in a vain attempt to neutralise the corpse due to the inherent risk of an XK-Class scenario if a containment breach were to occur. Unfortunately, his proposal is denied. He's given the usual spiel about how its a safe class object, how he'd be more at home at the Global Occult Coalition, about how historically attempted neutralisation of objects has often made things worse, which is why the Foundation contains rather than Destroy, Destroy, Destroy. The Site Director cites SCP-1609 as an example; it was a teleporting chair that the GOC put through a wood chipper. Now, it's a murderous pile of splinters.

What follows is a breach. An area of Site-19 becomes infected, and Beta-7 are deployed to clean up the mess, resulting in the death of Miller.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We discover that SCP-1609 (and many others) are completely fabricated. They don't exist. They are nothing but Foundation propaganda, a way to convince Foundation personnel that the GOC are incompetent and the Foundations way is the correct way… the only way, to deal with the anomalous. Moreover, they serve as a warning to those who would try to preemptively neutralise an anomalous object. The breach was orchestrated by the O5s to kill Miller after discovering the secret.

Additional Notes: Rough draft available on request.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Mechanical General
item.description: It's been a while, but I'm coming back with a new version of this SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Drama, History
Page Layout: The page will have the basic SCP article layout, but with addendums sharing the development of the general’s story.
Elevator Pitch: A sapient Gundam model. Has organs underneath the plastic armor plates, but they do not match any living species. The model speaks in memories of a fallen Vietnam War general that seems to be from a different timeline.
Central Narrative: Tells the story of an American Vietnam War General. A Gundam model was found in a former Vietnamese battlefield with significant damage. On the surface, there is nothing particularly strange about it. However, there appear to be functioning organs beneath the plastic armor plates that do not match up to any known species. Although they appear to be human-like, they contain DNA that varies greatly from those of humans. The model cannot move, but it is known to speak. It speaks from the perspective of General Richard Hall. The story it tells starts on November 8, 1955, and ends on May 9, 1961. It starts with Richard Hall getting drafted into the army. The story from there consists mostly of him giving orders to other soldiers or dialogue from his side only. At any points in time where a bodily fluid would come out of a person, the same thing happens to the model. For instance, real tears come out when Richard Hall cries. Recorded excretions include tears, sweat, blood, and urine. The majority of soldiers that Hall orders do not have records of being in the military. Although the story encompasses almost seven years, the full seven years are not played out. Only select days are played out. These days include battles, significant interactions, and promotions. The full day is always played out. On the final day, there is a battle in which Hall fights. We can tell that many soldiers are dying. The last thing said every time is "What the hell is that?" before the model starts bleeding profusely. After the bleeding stops, the story stops completely, and the model becomes dormant for 214 hours. After this, the story begins again the exact same way, in a cyclical nature. The real Richard Hall was a major, not a general. He died on July 24, 2006. Something turned him into a Gundam, but it is unknown what.
Hook: Emotional story told by a Gundam model.

item.title: Dr Cheese revamp :3
item.description: Hey ^^ This is the new version, as the old one was not clear in certain aspects. [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Page Layout: The usual SCP statements, Item Name, Item Class but no picture. Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signature, used for hunting. The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected. Suddenly, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. He got back to fixing the generator and replaced the fuses. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. He turned around, but there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. He was petrified, and sprinted out to the door and locked it shut. His frozen fingers dialled 911 into a telephone. The rest of the facility was wiped out, with the exception of Doctor Bradly who was obliterated by SCP-XXXX. Doctor Bradly called local authorities and the foundation was alerted. MTF unit Delta-92 Snow-and-Tell was sent to the situation immediately. Using infrared vision, the anomaly's ability was stunted, rendering it useless. Using a Class-3 collapsible containment cell, SCP-XXXX was taken to Site-25 via helicopter with ease.

item.title: Tales Of Jickery Woe Canon Idea
item.description: I need help on wondering if development is a good idea for this
item.content:encoded:
Hi! I'm new to this site, but not the SCP universe. Here is my idea, in what I hope will become a sprawling Canon.
Synopsis:

Welcome the 1930s. A specialist of biological warfare and weapon design, Jickery Woe, has taken in a destructive anomaly found washed up on the Santa Fe shores, and is preparing it for malicious purposes in the military. The Woe foundation quickly realizes, however, that this creature is unable to be contained. Using tracking devices developed for this creature, they begin to track down others. The Woe foundation struggles to keep the safety and peace of the nation, as SCP's begin to turn up everywhere. The Woe foundation eventually turns into the SCP foundation.

Notes:
While this is an SCP Canon, a big focus is on Jickery and his life.
I need able writers to make this come to pass.
Tell me what you think of this idea!

item.title: Vision Says "No" (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: An SCP that is impossible to look at. That's it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a human-like creature, around 6 feet tall. This is a SCP that is impossible to look at-not in the way of SCP-096 where if you look at its face, it will kill you, but as in the body will do everything it can to force a person not to look at it, e.g. making the person close their eyes, turning their head away, etc., similar to agnosia-this also effects photos and video recordings, not doing anything to alter them but still having the agnosia-type effect. The SCP is malevolent, and seems to be conscious of the effect it causes, as it constantly uses its inability to not be seen to anyone in the foundation to attempt escapes very frequently, making the containment not impossible, but very, very difficult.

Central Narrative: The foundation traces this SCP back to a road in an undisclosed town in Ohio, as specific section of the road had a sharp increase of traffic accidents for no apparent reason within 2-3 hours. After an investigative team gets there, they find nothing out of the ordinary except that they are physically unable to look down the center of the road. after pinpointing the center of the anomaly, they manage to find that the source of it is said SCP. The SCP goes along willingly, as this is its first encounter with the Foundation, but its anger towards them quickly ratchets up as strict containment procedures limit its freedom.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook of the story in my opinion is going to be mainly about the escape attempts of the SCP, as the foundation struggles to contain something impossible to look at and as the SCP finds new ways to trick the staff and exit, etc.

Additional Notes: This is not my first SCP Idea, but it is my first that I've gotten the courage to write up in here, so please tell me what is absolute garbage and what is ok

item.title: Killbox & Co.
item.description: A used car lot offering cars that kill their drivers.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): Description with interviews and a mission log

Elevator Pitch: A used car lot in Colorado that offers dirt-cheap classic autos. All owners crash fatally after a week of driving.

Central Narrative:
+ My first custom block
- Are you proud of me ma

The Foundation notices an absurdly sharp increase in automotive-related deaths tracing back to a single car lot and, after some investigating, designate it an anomaly, including all staff. Interview logs with staff members. Staff members don't require sustenance and at 10 pm sharp are all in their predetermined spots, sleeping. The next day their memory is reset. When talked to, they generally behave like normal humans and show very strong devotion to the car lot. Surveilance instated in a garage which provides the lot with its cars - proved futile as when a car appears, recording equipment malfunctions and witnesses black out. If anyone is seen approaching the garage, a staff member will warn them against it and become more and more agitated if subject doesn't move or refuse. Additionaly, other staff will begin to converge. If subject continues towards garage, staff will apprehend and throw them out. If subject gets into the garage, the salesman will say "Looks like the boss will take care of you now", upon which all exits to the garage close and Mr. Killbox enters the garage through a door leading to the main building. He is a 2.5 m brute with a mechanical arm made out of car parts. Shall the subject be caught, he will be killed and dragged behind the same door, which opens to an empty void for Killbox.
The staff will also start acting hostile if subject mentions Killbox by name or starts asking multiple questions in a row regarding the garage or the cars' origins.
Questions asked about the workers or the car lot will generally all result in answers like "The car lot is my life" and "I've worked here since as long as I can remember."
Staff have realistic human personalities, showing emotions and reacting as to be expected from regular humans. Their daily memory reset generally prevents them from developing critical thoughts. However, they are still capable of thinking freely (save for the instinctual response to trespassing into the garage).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Final Destination-style elaborate death setups.

Additional Notes: Crashes aim to also kill bystanders. Spectacularly. Hence the death toll.

item.title: The Chaos Insurgency is dead. Long live the Chaos Insurgency.
item.description: A tale of the Insurgency, the Afterlife Corbenic, and the big question //Why?//
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Bittersweet Political Thriller (if that's a thing)

Page Layout (Optional): Short story fragments, switching characters to spotlight the greater plot unfolding from different perspectives.

Elevator Pitch: Completely outnumbered and doubfounded by the Foundation going all-out during SCP-5000, the Insurgency tries to get the ☽☽☽-Initative to intervene.

Central Narrative: The cunning, but also very bold gambit of the CI to get the ☽☽☽-Initative into fighting the "Why?"-Foundation (which obviously fails), from them acquiring their first intel on Corbenic up to a forced "audience" infront of the Central Cabal, putting them into massive zugzwang. A somewhat different take on the fable of the mouse getting the bear to fight the fox.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Acting as misguided heroes/anti-villains and faced with an enemy they can't use brute force on, I want to emphazise all the other, non-violent subversive means by which they can coerce those mightier than them.

Additional Notes: If this idea seems crazy, that might be exactly it's appeal. Also, if this is any help, i'm not a greenhorn, I just prefered posting on my native branch and now try to get a foothold on the mainsite.
